purpose: Living architectural/design/theoretical/quality findings for a major refactoring phase after frontend parity. Record during every rewrite/port slice; do not expand current scope automatically.

policy.required_handoff: Update existing entry or add one with evidence, impact, current workaround, later proposal and validation; explicitly record none observed when applicable.
policy.certainty: Separate confirmed defect/limitation, supported design risk and hypothesis. Missing frontend implementation alone is not poor architecture.
policy.timing: Fix required behavior/contract correctness in current slice; defer broader structural cleanup. Never use deferred status to waive a frontend acceptance gate.
policy.deduplication: Stable RF IDs, append new evidence and affected workflows rather than duplicate entries.
policy.closure: Retain history with fix/decision/source/evidence; do not delete embarrassing findings or mark solved from a plan.

findings.title: Shared presentation and Runtime are integration hotspots
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: The current presentation spans 1,399 lines and Runtime 960 lines, with shell, workspace routing, data/service actions and lifecycle integration sharing these modules. The reference Workbench is 1,426 lines. Length alone is not a defect; the concrete cost is that independent workflow edits repeatedly touch the same ownership surface.
findings.impact: Concurrent changes can conflict, and a one-to-one port could preserve broad coupling between workspace controls and service lifecycles.
findings.during_port: Use private feature modules with one coordinator owning shared composition; avoid a general framework before useful screens land.
findings.post_port_proposal: After parity, assess stable workspace/host orchestration modules with narrow interfaces and one authoritative session.
findings.validation_needed: Measure cross-workflow files changed for a representative feature and show that isolated workflow edits/tests no longer require unrelated shell/runtime changes.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

handoff_evidence.observation: Saved Library presentation deep-copied accepted ProjectDoc and all saved documents on Runtime repaints. Bounded correction uses existing immutable Arc document snapshots and borrows saved-list signal. Strict WASM Clippy passes; browser review pending; allocation latency remains unmeasured.
handoff_evidence.status: current correction under review; retain immutable presentation ownership/allocation follow-up

findings.title: Internal browser host types are exposed as crate APIs
findings.confidence: confirmed observation; future cost is a design risk
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: web exports cad_jobs, renderer_host and several host modules publicly; CadOperation/CadRequest and wrapper methods are public. Adding a seemingly internal operation can therefore widen a Rust crate surface even when wire/file semantics stay unchanged. The page binary separately declares Runtime/presentation and imports the boardstudio_web library: pub(crate) in that library is not callable from the binary. Private wrapper placement must account for the actual crate boundary.
findings.impact: Implementation detail and intentional compatibility contract are hard to distinguish; private adapter evolution can trigger unnecessary broad API decisions.
findings.during_port: Place a private wrapper in the same crate as its consumer, or use an already sufficient public facade. Verify library-to-binary reachability before declaring a pub(crate) wrapper feasible; any needed public expansion remains an explicit decision.
findings.post_port_proposal: Audit actual consumers, explicitly separate stable public contracts from host internals, and propose compatible deprecation/module boundaries rather than silently shrinking visibility.
findings.validation_needed: List real external consumers and compile compatibility fixtures; prove internal operation changes no longer alter the intended public surface.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

follow_up_evidence.observation: Public BrowserStore discovery returns only Vec<ProjectDoc> or aggregate error, so private page callers cannot retain identified damaged cards and healthy records after typed deserialization fails. The existing raw storage helper/database identity are private in another crate.
follow_up_evidence.certainty: confirmed source boundary limitation; tolerant discovery proposal not applied or approved
follow_up_evidence.current_mitigation: Keep per-card typed geometry fallback private; prepare smallest additive read-only discovery API for explicit decision. Do not fake documents, skip records or duplicate writable storage authority.
follow_up_evidence.post_port_follow_up: Evaluate host discovery/read-model depth and safe degraded presentation contracts after port.
follow_up_evidence.validation: Real isolated mixed healthy/damaged/unusable-identity rows, strict-open and unchanged schema/API behavior; transaction errors and stale list guards.

findings.title: CAD engine capabilities and host protocols drift apart
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Rust WASM already exports build_keycaps, but the Dioxus host/worker operation set covers case preview/exact/STEP/read only. The initial review mistook the absent host path for a missing provider until the engine export was traced.
findings.impact: Capabilities can be overlooked, duplicated, or falsely described as backend work; behavior and cancellation can diverge between host wrappers.
findings.during_port: BND.1 proves the private keycap worker adapter using the existing engine; retain reference chunk/yield and revision/ID semantics.
findings.post_port_proposal: Create an explicit capability-to-host contract map and shared conformance fixtures for required engine operations; consider reducing duplicated wrapper protocol knowledge.
findings.validation_needed: Every required capability has a verified engine→worker→host→UI trace, same fixture outputs and cancellation/error disposition.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

findings.title: Immutable export tokens do not model export-owned commits
findings.confidence: confirmed contract mismatch for PCB workflow
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Session export captures an immutable token and cancels registered exports on accepted commits. React PCB export deliberately adopts its own wiring and protection commits, with packaging before protection, while unrelated changes invalidate output.
findings.impact: A naive port either cancels its own valid export or weakens stale-output guards. Ownership of a multi-step operation and its accepted document lineage is not represented uniformly.
findings.during_port: BND.2 must prove safe private operation/commit correlation; preserve ordering and reject all unrelated changes. If impossible through existing contracts, record a concrete API proposal before dependent code.
findings.post_port_proposal: Evaluate explicit operation lineage/transaction ownership across session jobs, edits, persistence and artifact delivery, with a documented consistency model.
findings.validation_needed: Race matrix: owned versus unrelated commits, save failure, navigation, cancellation and packaging failure; no stale delivery and no protection without successful packaging.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

findings.title: Geometric edit planning lives in frontend helper policy
findings.confidence: confirmed remaining TS policy; target placement is a hypothesis
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Resize/reflow computes canonical linked-half deduplication, axis projections, spacing and center preservation in TS UI helpers. No equivalent callable Rust resize/reflow controller was found, although core owns matrix projection and accepted edits.
findings.impact: A component-only rewrite would lose behavior or leave hidden TS logic; moving the policy carelessly could duplicate geometry authority.
findings.during_port: F6C.3 ports the existing policy into a private Rust frontend controller with preserved helper/public workflow tests and one normal edit/history path.
findings.post_port_proposal: After parity, decide whether interaction planning belongs in a dedicated application service using core geometry primitives, with explicit draft/commit ownership.
findings.validation_needed: Compare identical resize traces across pointer/keyboard, mixed selections and linked boards; no semantic drift, duplicated calculations or extra history steps.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

follow_up_evidence.observation: The reference selection controller carries matrix/row/column context and computes an anchored live-member rectangle. The current Dioxus caller supplies flat visible part IDs to a Session Range operation that selects their linear interval and advances its anchor. Semantic tree context is absent from the read model. This extends the frontend interaction-policy ownership finding beyond resize/reflow.
follow_up_evidence.certainty: source-confirmed behavior mismatch; public regression reproduction remains required
follow_up_evidence.current_mitigation: Proposed T1-10 proves a private semantic-context adapter while Session keeps real part selection. T1-12 first reproduces the rectangle/anchor mismatch, then Astra repairs the bounded behavior using existing contracts.
follow_up_evidence.post_port_follow_up: Review one explicit home for matrix selection context, anchor policy and part-ID membership, avoiding overlapping writable selection stores.
follow_up_evidence.validation: Paired range traces with repeated Shift, toggles, empty/disabled cells and board switches; no fabricated part IDs, stale scope or extra document revisions.

findings.title: Canonical, physical-instance and isolated sample scopes are easy to conflate
findings.confidence: confirmed distinct scopes; abstraction improvement is a hypothesis
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Layout/Keymap/Keycaps use canonical boards; Case projects a physical instance; Parts builds an isolated sample. Authored Case STEP uses canonical saved bodies while generated mechanical export explicitly projects the instance. All may share viewer and artifact code.
findings.impact: A generic board/instance argument or copied projection rule can mirror the wrong geometry, leak a sample into the document, or export the wrong scope.
findings.during_port: Use one shared viewer with explicit consumer inputs; preserve each reference projection and captured identity. Test cross-scope switches and stale replies.
findings.post_port_proposal: Evaluate typed scope/projection inputs and coordinate-frame invariants for view, edit and export consumers; separate display projection from saved-document identity.
findings.validation_needed: Table-driven fixtures for front/back/split/instance/sample scopes plus properties for stable IDs, reflection count, unchanged canonical document and correct outputs.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

findings.title: Runtime observation currently supports one subscriber
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Runtime subscribe assigns a single notifier and unsubscribe clears it. This supports the current root composition but is not an independently mountable multi-consumer subscription contract.
findings.impact: If feature modules subscribe directly, one may replace another or remove notification delivery on unmount. No present lost-update bug is claimed.
findings.during_port: Keep the existing root subscription and pass projections/callbacks to children; do not give each workspace an independent subscription.
findings.post_port_proposal: Assess a scoped subscription lifecycle or explicit root reactive projection after measuring actual needs; avoid adding an event bus by default.
findings.validation_needed: Mount/unmount and rapid switching with two observers in a characterization probe; verify ownership and no stale/lost notification or redundant large clone.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

findings.title: Archive packing capability is split from its UI options and asset resolution
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: React copy always includes local assets and optionally discovers/embeds used bundled models with the project-name filename. Runtime packing currently includes document.assets and delivers keyboard.boardstudio without that option.
findings.impact: The same visible copy action can produce archives with different portability and naming across entrypoints/hosts.
findings.during_port: F2.2 owns one shared packing action with correct asset semantics; F8 owns its route checkbox/button. Preserve formats, IDs and hashes.
findings.post_port_proposal: Unify explicit archive input/options and asset-source resolution responsibilities with one compatibility test corpus across hosts.
findings.validation_needed: Reference/candidate round trips with imported assets, bundled used models enabled/disabled, missing asset failures and identical project-name output.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

follow_up_evidence.observation: Demo fixture opening currently reuses archive import, which submits the parsed project identity unchanged, whereas React demo constructors allocate a fresh project ID. A fixture reopen therefore must not be assumed to have editable-copy identity semantics.
follow_up_evidence.certainty: source-supported copy-identity risk; repeated-open browser reproduction not yet performed
follow_up_evidence.current_mitigation: Proposed T1-04 characterizes repeated demo starts and preserves prior edited copies through a private demo action. Confirmed defects go to Astra; ordinary archive-import identity semantics must remain unchanged.
follow_up_evidence.post_port_follow_up: Separate explicit open-existing/import-archive/start-demo-copy intent and identity ownership while sharing archive validation and asset transport.
follow_up_evidence.validation: Start the same demo twice, edit/save each, and independently reopen both with identical intended asset references; stale/failing starts cannot replace later work.

findings.title: Parity accounting and acceptance evidence are scattered

Existing browser suites target React, bounded Dioxus evidence lives in task artifacts, and historical visual references are only in the original checkout. Actual screen-reader coverage is unavailable on this host.
findings.impact: Plans and passing partial checks can imply unsupported completeness; evidence may not identify the delivered source and environment consistently.
findings.during_port: Maintain the source/task/evidence ledger and public Dioxus scenarios during the port; resolve actual AT and applicable release gates before frontend adoption.
findings.post_port_proposal: After parity, consolidate maintained conformance scenarios, source/fixture/build provenance and CI integration; treat evidence as reproducible outputs rather than accumulated prose.
findings.validation_needed: From one commit, locate every required workflow scenario and produce its current result with exact source/build/fixture identity and explicit unavailable gates.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry

findings.title: Cancellation has different guarantees at worker and kernel boundaries
findings.confidence: confirmed limitation; not automatically a design defect
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Preview can yield between keycap chunks; a synchronous WASM STEP build cannot be interrupted mid-kernel call. Host cancellation can stop queued work and suppress stale completion without immediately releasing ongoing computation.
findings.impact: A single cancelled status can obscure remaining CPU/memory work or lead the UI to promise prompt preemption that the engine does not provide.
findings.during_port: Preserve chunk/yield preview behavior and late-result suppression; report actual cancellation granularity, keep resource checks and do not add unproven preemption claims.
findings.post_port_proposal: Review cancellation contracts, scheduling/resource budgets and operation status terminology across host/worker/kernel; evaluate cooperative work units only with measured benefit.
findings.validation_needed: Measure cancel-to-settle and retained resources for queued, chunked preview and synchronous export; verify no stale scene/file even when computation finishes after cancellation.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

follow_up_evidence.certainty: confirmed public defect; delayed real request and already-executed reply both reproduce
follow_up_evidence.observation: Runtime guards saved-document loading by sequence but Session adoption/persistence lacks latest open intent. Pending A adopts and changes durable active project after newer B is unavailable. No-B control opens A normally.
follow_up_evidence.current_mitigation: Full ticket acceptance remains blocked; pure UI and independent panels/tree continue. No unsafe reply dropping, fabricated core error, history-resetting restore or narrower acceptance applied.
follow_up_evidence.post_port_follow_up: Review cancellation/adoption contracts across UI intent, worker state, durable commit and one-time caller settlement.
follow_up_evidence.validation: Retained red-capable public loop plus pending-core/save variants, valid/unavailable B and history/selection retention; repaired source needs independent review.

findings.title: CAD revision envelope has a JavaScript safe-integer ceiling
findings.confidence: confirmed CAD-only technical limit; low-probability scale risk
findings.observation: MAX_CAD_REVISION is 9,007,199,254,740,991 and larger CAD revisions are explicitly rejected because that worker boundary uses JS numbers. This is specific to CAD and does not negate the separately verified exact core/archive integer transport.
findings.impact: The CAD identity domain is narrower than the document integer domain; practical lifetime relevance needs evidence.
findings.during_port: Preserve explicit rejection and existing boundary tests; never round a revision or weaken stale checks.
findings.post_port_proposal: Audit whether this limit matters; only if warranted consider string/bigint identity across the CAD envelope with compatibility handling.
findings.validation_needed: Max/max+1 request/reply tests and realistic revision growth estimate before changing representation.

findings.title: Object tree containers have invalid required-child semantics
findings.confidence: confirmed inherited critical axe violation in the Dioxus candidate and pinned React reference
findings.status: open; no accessibility waiver; candidate acceptance gate remains required; private semantics repair f65b is under independent review and is not integrated or accepted
findings.observation: Axe 4.12.1 reports the critical aria-required-children violation in both paired applications: the candidate .m1-component-list role=tree directly contains labelled disclosure buttons, and the React .wb-tree-viewport role=tree has the same invalid child pattern. The candidate report has one critical violation; the React report has the same critical violation plus a separate moderate page-has-heading-one finding. The shared result identifies an inherited reference defect; it does not establish candidate conformance or waive accessibility acceptance. A private candidate semantics repair exists at f65b and is under independent review; it is neither merged nor accepted and does not close this finding.
findings.impact: Assistive technologies may not receive the required tree/treeitem structure for object hierarchy navigation. The axe impact is critical and remains an active correctness gate.
findings.during_port: Do not suppress the rule, weaken the threshold or accept the candidate because the reference shares the defect. Correct candidate tree semantics while preserving hierarchy, selection and keyboard behavior; retain both reports as paired baseline evidence. Actual assistive-technology testing remains separately required where applicable.
findings.post_port_proposal: Review the tree semantic structure and maintained accessibility conformance scenario across workspace navigation; keep the eventual design narrow and compatible with tree disclosure and selection behavior.
findings.validation_needed: Axe reports no aria-required-children violation on the candidate; public hierarchy, selection, keyboard and focus behavior remain correct; retain the React report as evidence of the inherited baseline defect. Actual assistive-technology evidence is a separate gate.
findings.decision: current acceptance gate; no waiver and no parent closure
findings.follow_up_owner: T1-10/F3.1 implementation and independent accessibility review
